bill.title: Protecting Children with Food Allergies Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry. (text: CR S2568)
bill.officialSummary: Protecting Children with Food Allergies Act of 2025 This bill requires that local school food service personnel receive annual training and certification on food allergies as part of the training provided by the National School Lunch Program of the Department of Agriculture. Under current law, the mandatory training and certification for school food service personnel must include modules on (1) nutrition, and (2) health and food safety standards and methodologies. Under the bill, the training and certification must also include a module on food allergies, including information on the best practices to prevent, recognize, and respond to food-related allergic reactions. As part of the certification, the bill also requires that food service personnel demonstrate competence in the training provided.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would require school cafeteria workers participating in the National School Lunch Program to complete annual training on food allergies. The training would cover how to prevent allergic reactions, recognize symptoms, and respond appropriately. Workers would need to demonstrate competence in this training as part of their certification, adding to existing requirements for nutrition and food safety training.

industries.rationale: School systems operating lunch programs would face new training and certification requirements for food service staff.
Food service companies and contractors providing school meals would need to ensure staff meet the new allergen training standards.

plain.whatItDoes: This bill would require that local school food service personnel receive annual training and certification on food allergies as part of the training provided by the National School Lunch Program of the USDA.
plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in farming, and food prices. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
